title: Feed A Crowd: Vego Chilli and Herby Rice
subtitle: Cook Once, Serve More!
description: Serve up more with our Feed A Crowd recipes! Using the same amount of protein but with more hearty ingredients like filling carbs and veggies, you can satisfy extra hungry tummies or keep something for tomorrow’s lunch. If you’re on a 2-person plan, these recipes make 4 portions; on a 4-person plan, they make 8 portions.

steps.text: Cook rice: Fill a large saucepan three-quarters full with water and bring to the boil. Add the rice and cook for 12 mins or until tender. Drain. Return to the pan and cover to keep warm.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, coarsely chop the capsicums. Quarter the carrots lengthwise and thinly slice. Reserve a few coriander sprigs, then finely chop the leaves and stems, keeping them separate. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the beans.

Start chilli: Heat 1 tbs olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook the capsicum and carrot, stirring occasionally, for 5-6 mins until softened. Add the Tex-Mex seasoning (see Did you know?), coriander stems, garlic and 2 tbs tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant.

Simmer chilli: Add the tomatoes, beans and 125ml (½ cup) water to the veggies and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 5-7 mins until the sauce is slightly reduced. Increase the heat to high and cook for a further 2-3 mins until thickened. Remove the pan from the heat. Stir 2 tsp soy sauce and 2 tsp sugar into the chilli. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve up: Add the chopped coriander leaves to the rice and fluff with a fork. Divide the coriander rice and vego chilli among bowls. Scatter over the reserved coriander sprigs and enjoy!

Did you know?: You've probably heard of chilli con carne, but have you heard of chilli sin carne? It's chilli but without the meat. Our version is made with capsicum, carrots, mixed beans and tomatoes – and even though it's called 'chilli', there's no chilli in it, just a bit of spiciness in the Tex-Mex seasoning.
